TS-CP2 change point model

Source: R/cpd_members.R
tscp2.Rd

Trains the unsupervised TS-CP2 model of Deldari et al. (2021), as re-implemented in the WWAggr code: a temporal convolutional network (TCN) embeds windows of window steps; it is trained with a contrastive (InfoNCE-like) loss so that each history window is close to the window that follows it and far from the other windows of the batch. The change score of a step is 1 minus the cosine similarity of the embeddings of the two consecutive windows that end at it (see cpd_scores()).

Usage

tscp2(
  x,
  window = 4,
  nb_filters = 64,
  kernel_size = 5,
  nb_stacks = 2,
  dilations = c(1, 2, 4, 8),
  use_skip_connections = TRUE,
  batch_norm = FALSE,
  n_steps = 8,
  code_size = 4,
  temperature = 0.1,
  learning_rate = 0.001,
  decay_steps = 1000,
  batch_size = 8,
  epochs = 200,
  patience = 5,
  min_delta = 1e-04,
  step = 1,
  alpha = 1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Training sequences, in the formats accepted by indid(). Only the first 2 * window steps of every sequence are used (a history window and the future window that follows it).

window

Length of the history and future windows.

nb_filters

Number of filters of the convolutions.

kernel_size

Kernel size of the convolutions.

nb_stacks, dilations

The TCN has nb_stacks stacks of residual blocks, one per dilation.

use_skip_connections

Whether the skip connection of the last block is added to the output of the TCN.

batch_norm

Whether the convolutions are followed by batch normalisation.

n_steps, code_size

Sizes of the dense layers: 2 * n_steps, n_steps and the embedding (code_size).

temperature

Temperature of the contrastive loss.

learning_rate

Learning rate of Adam, annealed by a cosine schedule of period decay_steps epochs.

decay_steps

Period of the cosine annealing (T_max, in epochs).

batch_size

Number of sequences per batch.

epochs

Largest number of epochs.

patience, min_delta

Early stopping on the training loss: training stops after patience epochs whose loss is not below the best one minus min_delta.

step, alpha

Prediction settings: the similarity is computed every step steps, and the scores are smoothed by an exponential moving average with factor alpha (1: none).

seed

Seed of the private random stream (initial weights and order of the batches). NULL draws one from the session.

Value

A tscp2 object with the parameters, the batch normalisation statistics, the settings and the training loss of every epoch.

Details

The model follows the reference code (https://github.com/stalex2902/wwagr-ensemble-cpd, src/baselines/tscp.py and prediction_utils.py):

  • Every residual block is a causal dilated convolution, ReLU, a second one, ReLU, plus the input (through a 1x1 convolution when the number of channels changes), then ReLU. Convolution weights are initialised from N(0, 0.05) with zero biases.

  • The window [window, channels] is reshaped (not transposed) to [channels, window] before the TCN, as x.reshape(batch, -1, seq_len) of the reference.

  • The loss of a batch of N pairs is the binary cross-entropy (target 1) of the logits sum_i exp(s_ii / temperature) / sum_j exp(s_ij / temperature), where s_ij is the cosine similarity of history i and future j.

  • The scores are 1 - max(s, 0) (Appendix B of the WWAggr paper).

The dropout of the reference (rate 0 in its configurations) and its layer and weight normalisation options (not functional there) are not implemented. The network, its gradients and Adam are written in R. The defaults are those of the Human Activity configuration of the reference (configs/human_activity_tscp.yaml).

References

Deldari, S., Smith, D. V., Xue, H. and Salim, F. D. (2021). Time series change point detection with self-supervised contrastive predictive coding. Proceedings of The Web Conference 2021, 3124-3135. doi:10.1145/3442381.3449903

Stepikin, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2025). WWAggr: A window Wasserstein-based aggregation for ensemble change point detection. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 1535-1544. doi:10.1109/ICDM65498.2025.00163

See also

cpd_scores(), cpd_ensemble(), dfr_wwaggr().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- array(stats::rnorm(16 * 12 * 2), c(16, 12, 2))
model <- tscp2(x, window = 4, nb_filters = 4, dilations = c(1, 2), n_steps = 4, code_size = 3,
               epochs = 3, seed = 1)
model
#> TS-CP2 model: windows of 4 steps, 2 feature(s), embedding of size 3, 3 epoch(s)
